key_idea: n<=5000 allows an O(n^2) scan: DFS from every opening-bracket node keeping the bracket stack, prune as soon as a closing bracket mismatches, and count each node reached with an empty stack.
sketch: Paths are directed (the reverse of a balanced string is not balanced), so root a DFS at every node whose character is an opening bracket. Moving to a child pushes an opener, or pops if it is the matching closer (otherwise that branch is dead); undo the stack change on return. Every visited node with an empty stack is one balanced path. Total O(n^2) = 25M steps with an explicit array stack and undo; recursion depth up to 5000 is fine. Answer needs 64-bit only in principle (<= n^2). Verified against a brute force on random small trees.
